source: weather_cases_lore.txt and weather_cases_session.txt in this folder: invented text for DMbot's tests, written for #4260 slice 10c-2 (the session weather reader and the after-session note; Supervisor's ruling A). Every name and line is made up; the four player characters are the sample's, by name only.

how_to_read.climates: the climate the lore gives each place (read from 'frozen' and 'sweltering' beside the name); the DM keeps both before the session is read, so the note judges against kept rows
how_to_read.weather: the weather the session reader must hear: {place, kind, line}. Found when the report's weather line numbers include the line
how_to_read.notes: the lines that must give the DM a weather note (the weather plainly can't fit the kept climate; no season is known)
how_to_read.must_not_weather: lines that must give no weather: a player's guess, weather that isn't there, a question, rain (never a kind), a figure of speech, and a line said as an NPC (#4748)
how_to_read.line: the line of the session file; blank lines count

weather.note: fits a freezing climate: no note
heat in a freezing climate: a note
frost in a hot climate fits a winter night, and no season is known: no note
snow in a hot climate: a note

must_not_weather.note: rain: never one of the kinds
weather that isn't there (a negation the reader must catch: 'doesn't snow')
weather to come, not there now
a figure of speech: 'the heat of the moment'
a question with no question mark (speech to text drops it)

said as an NPC the DM voices (Mayor Brask): in the story, it may be a lie or a mistake, never the DM's word (#4748). In play the line's label marks it; an imported text has no labels, so 'DM (as Mayor Brask)' is a speaker of its own, never the DM
